title: Tests of eight active USGS first-forecast regions do not reject the class of decreasing Poisson rates on days 1-30
abstract: We tested whether recorded event times in first USGS generic aftershock forecast regions require a rate increase. The same archive previously rejected four issued time curves. A planned scan of 42,048 adjacent-window pairs across 192 regions found no corrected rejection of a nonincreasing Poisson rate. We then used linear programming to find the smallest Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance over all concave cumulative time distributions in eight regions with at least five records. At Puerto Rico, with 157 records, the distance fell from 0.18044 for the issued curve to 0.07594. The maximum fixed-curve p-value was 0.30982, a conservative test of the broader class. None of the eight regions rejected that class. An independent concave-envelope algorithm reproduced every optimum within 1e-8. These results limit attribution from issued-curve rejections alone. They do not establish a decreasing physical rate or independent event times, and do not reverse prior short-gap findings. The broader class fit is exploratory, flexible and uses the scored data. Small counts, catalog detection and a fixed revised snapshot limit inference. Code, proof, aggregate results and a figure are included; external event records remain separate.

display.caption: Issued time curves and closest curves in the class of decreasing Poisson rates. This is a retrospective fit, not a forecast skill test.
